# Practice Problems
Problem one asks students to analyze a recurrence tree and justify each level cost.
Problem one asks for a clear recurrence tree argument instead of a memorized formula.
Problem one also asks students to explain where the combine work appears and how many subproblems exist per level.
Problem one rewards grounded reasoning about repeated expansion, leaf count, and why the total work can be summed safely.
Problem one keeps the practice style close to lecture notes so retrieval should surface both assignment and notes evidence.

## Graph Cut Exercise
This assignment asks students to find a graph cut after computing a max flow.
The graph cut exercise focuses on reachable vertices, residual edges, and cut capacity.
The graph cut exercise asks for a short explanation of why the chosen cut is valid after the flow computation finishes.
The graph cut exercise uses the same vocabulary as the notes: reachable set, sink side, and boundary capacity.
The graph cut exercise is intended to produce practice-question style retrieval for the regression harness.
